facets.description: Whether the context identifies the modeled subject and establishes the semantic inside/outside boundary needed to classify in-scope use cases and external actors without requiring a visible subject box.

ratingAnchors.0: No selected claim or accepted assumption identifies the modeled subject or any usable inside/outside boundary.
ratingAnchors.1: A selected input names a possible system, subsystem, or domain, but its modeled level or boundary cannot be determined reliably.
ratingAnchors.2: The subject is identifiable, but its level, included responsibilities, exclusions, or the classification of one or more in-scope use cases or external actors is absent or ambiguous.
ratingAnchors.3: The modeled system, subsystem, or domain and its semantic inside/outside boundary are established well enough to classify every confirmed in-scope use case as subject behavior and every participating actor as external; a visible subject box is not required.
ratingAnchors.4: Rating 3 is met without assumptions, and the subject level, included responsibilities, exclusions, and external responsibilities are explicit, complete, precise, and unambiguous.

facets.description: Whether the context identifies the external human roles and external systems that participate in the subject's confirmed in-scope goals and distinguishes them from internal components.

ratingAnchors.0: No selected claim or accepted assumption identifies an external human role or external system that participates in an in-scope goal.
ratingAnchors.1: A selected input names a possible participant, but its external status, role, or participation in the subject cannot be determined reliably.
ratingAnchors.2: At least one external role or system is established, but one or more participants required by the confirmed in-scope goals is absent or ambiguous, roles are conflated, or an internal component may be misclassified as external.
ratingAnchors.3: Every external human role and external system required by the confirmed in-scope goals is identified, roles are distinct where their goals or participation differ, and internal controllers, repositories, and other implementation components are excluded.
ratingAnchors.4: Rating 3 is met without assumptions, and every role boundary, external-system status, and distinct participant responsibility is explicit, complete, precise, and unambiguous.

facets.description: Whether the context identifies the user-visible outcomes or capabilities sought from the subject for every confirmed in-scope actor intent at the requested abstraction level.

ratingAnchors.0: No selected claim or accepted assumption establishes a user-visible outcome or capability sought from the subject.
ratingAnchors.1: A selected input hints at an actor intent or subject capability, but no reliable user-visible goal can be stated.
ratingAnchors.2: At least one user-visible goal is established, but one or more confirmed in-scope actor intents lacks an outcome, has an ambiguous boundary, is expressed only as an implementation step or incidental UI action, or is at the wrong abstraction level.
ratingAnchors.3: Every confirmed in-scope actor intent is expressed as a bounded user-visible outcome or capability at the requested abstraction level, with implementation steps and incidental UI actions excluded as substitute goals.
ratingAnchors.4: Rating 3 is met without assumptions, and every in-scope goal boundary, outcome, distinction, and abstraction level is explicit, complete, precise, and unambiguous.

facets.description: Whether the context explicitly establishes which external actors participate in which confirmed in-scope goals rather than inferring participation from actor and goal existence.

ratingAnchors.0: No selected claim or accepted assumption establishes a usable participation connection between an external actor and an in-scope goal.
ratingAnchors.1: A selected input suggests that an actor and goal are related, but the participant, goal, or participation proposition cannot be determined reliably.
ratingAnchors.2: At least one actor-goal participation connection is established, but one or more confirmed in-scope goals is orphaned, a required participant is absent or ambiguous, or a connection relies only on separate actor and goal existence.
ratingAnchors.3: Every confirmed in-scope goal is connected to each participating external actor established by the selected context, no in-scope goal is orphaned, and every connection identifies both its actor and goal endpoints.
ratingAnchors.4: Rating 3 is met without assumptions, and participation is explicit, complete, precise, and unambiguous for every supported in-scope actor-goal combination.

facets.description: Whether the context establishes requested or in-scope include, extend, actor generalization, use-case generalization, and named extension-point meaning, including a standalone request for named extension points, with the participants, direction, conditions, locations, names, and ownership required by each included concept.

appliesWhenAny: The confirmed request explicitly asks to depict an include relationship between identified use cases.
The confirmed request explicitly asks to depict an extend relationship between identified use cases.
The confirmed request explicitly asks to depict generalization between identified actors or between identified use cases.
The confirmed request explicitly asks for one or more named extension points on an identified use case, including a standalone extension-point request that does not ask for an extend relationship.
An included-scope decision, selected claim, or accepted assumption asserts one of those relationships or assigns a named extension point to an identified use case.
A relevant active-index claim asserts one of those relationships or assigns a named extension point to an identified use case within the requested subject and scope.
An open uncertainty states that one of those relationships or a named extension point is in confirmed scope but leaves required relationship or extension-point details unresolved.
notApplicableWhenAll: The confirmed request does not ask to depict include, extend, actor generalization, use-case generalization, or a named extension point.
No included-scope decision, selected claim, or accepted assumption asserts any of those relationships or assigns a named extension point to an identified use case.
No relevant active-index claim asserts any of those relationships or assigns a named extension point to an identified use case within the requested subject and scope.
No open uncertainty states that one of those relationships or a named extension point is or may be in the confirmed scope.
Every explicit scope exclusion of those concepts is coherent with the confirmed goal and relevant indexed claims.
uncertainWhen: A request phrase, selected input, relevant active-index claim, or open uncertainty indicates that one of the listed concepts may belong in the diagram but does not establish whether the confirmed scope includes or excludes it.
The confirmed request or an explicit scope exclusion conflicts with selected or indexed context about whether one of the listed concepts belongs in scope.

ratingAnchors.0: The facet is applicable, but no selected claim or accepted assumption establishes any usable include, extend, actor generalization, use-case generalization, or named extension-point meaning.
ratingAnchors.1: A selected input hints at one of the applicable concepts, but its relationship kind, participants, endpoint roles, direction, condition, location, extension-point name, or owning use case cannot be determined reliably.
ratingAnchors.2: At least one applicable concept is established in part, but an in-scope item lacks one or more details required to model it: include endpoints or direction; extend endpoints, direction, condition, or extension location; generalization child, parent, or direction; or a named extension point's exact name or owning use case.
ratingAnchors.3: Every in-scope item is modelable: include identifies the including and included use cases and direction; extend identifies the extending and base use cases, direction, condition, and extension location; generalization identifies the specialized and parent actor or use case and direction; and each named extension point identifies its exact name and owning use case. Only clauses for concepts present in scope apply, and a standalone named extension-point request does not require an extend relationship.
ratingAnchors.4: Rating 3 is met without assumptions, and every in-scope relationship kind, endpoint role, direction, extend condition and location, generalization child/parent distinction, and named extension-point name and ownership is explicit, complete, precise, and unambiguous.
